# Documentation lives in two places — keep both current

`mbdeploy` is documented on two sites that deliberately split public from private.
**Both must be updated when you make a major change.** They cross-reference each
other, so an agent that lands on either one can reach the other.

| Site | Scope | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| <https://robots.jointheleague.org/subsystems/mbdeploy/> | The manual — concepts, commands, protocols, generic deployment. **No machine specifics.** | `docs/wiki/` **in this repo** |
| <http://robot-garage.home/doku.php?id=mbdeploy> | The machines — hosts, IPs, SSH, per-node install paths, current daemon status. Garage LAN only. | The DokuWiki page itself |

## The rule

After any change that alters observable behaviour — a new subcommand or flag, a
changed wire protocol, a new dependency, a changed install or deployment
procedure, a fixed defect a user could have hit — **update the docs in the same
piece of work, not later**:

1. **`docs/wiki/`** for anything about how the tool behaves. Each `docs/wiki/*.md`
   is one published page and needs `title:` and `blurb:` front matter; bump its
   `updated:` date. Files starting with `_` are not published.
   Keep `docs/wiki/index.md` (`order: 0`) as the map — it links the pages and
   carries the open-tasks / known-gaps list.
2. **The Robot Garage wiki page** for anything about the fleet itself — a node
   added or removed, a board moved, an install path or service change, a node
   whose daemon is down. Its "Current status" table goes stale fastest and is the
   thing an agent trusts most.
3. If you changed what one site says about the other, fix the cross-link too.

Never put hostnames, IP addresses, SSH keys, or per-node paths into `docs/wiki/` —
that is what the internal wiki is for, and the public site is world-readable.

## How publishing works

The hub *pulls* `docs/wiki/` from this repo and renders it; nothing is pushed to
the hub, and the hub never writes here. Changes under `docs/wiki/**` trigger
`.github/workflows/notify-docs-hub.yml`, which pings the hub to rebuild.

Caveat specific to this repo: the notify workflow authenticates with a
League-Robotics org GitHub App, and this repo lives at `Busboombot/mbdeploy`,
outside that org — so the ping step will not have the org secrets and will fail.
The hub still picks the docs up on its next build, and an admin can trigger one
manually. Registration lives in `subsystems.yml` in
`League-Robotics/League-Robotics.github.io` (branch `master`); public repos are
cloned anonymously, so being outside the org does not block *pulling*.

The complete publishing contract is at <https://robots.jointheleague.org/publishing/>.

## Hardware safety rule — do not flash the NEZHA2 robots

Standing instruction from the stakeholder. On the Robot Garage fleet, boards whose
registry `role` is `NEZHA2` are working robots running firmware people depend on.

- `connect` / `connect --remote` — **allowed** on any board, NEZHA2 included. It holds
  DTR low, so opening the port does not reset the board.
- `deploy` / `deploy --remote` — **never** target a `NEZHA2` board, and never pick one
  as the test target when working on the flash path. Use a **silent** board (empty
  `role`) instead; `mbdeploy list --remote` shows the ROLE column.

The relay guard does **not** protect these: it only refuses roles naming a relay or
bridge. Nothing in the tool prevents flashing a robot — this rule is the only thing
that does.
